newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: MOTOR RACING-WILLIAMS ON TOP BUT IRVINE SEES NEW FERRARI ERA.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-WILLIAMS ON TOP BUT IRVINE SEES NEW FERRARI ERA.

text.p: Jacques Villeneuve may have flown home with a 10-point lead in the world drivers' championship but his old rival Eddie Irvine signalled a new era for Ferrari by finishing second behind him in Sunday's Argentine Grand Prix.

Irvine, 31, was only nine-tenths of a second behind the 26-year-old Canadian when they crossed the line and afterwards he said the result would be a boost to him and the Italian team ahead of their 'home' race at Imola in two weeks' time.

"I came into this race needing a decent finish and that is exactly what I got," the Briton said. "But it was good for the team as well as for me. I think it really could signal the start of a new era now for Ferrari."
Irvine's best-ever finish came after his Ferrari team mate and double world champion Michael Schumacher had retired following another first-corner collision.

"That gave me the chance to shine a bit without Michael in the race and I just went for it," said Irvine. "The car was great and really reliable. I think we have a good package and it is going to be interesting from now on."
Irvine and Schumacher both said they felt confident about the team's prospects for the San Marino Grand Prix at Imola later this month.

Irvine said: "Things are starting to go my way now, at long last. It's been a long while coming but it has been worth the wait. I've been unlucky. Some days things go your way and some days they don't."
Despite pressure from the Italian media, Ferrari resisted calls before the Argentine Grand Prix to consider Irvine's future with the team after poor results in the opening two races of the season.
Irvine said: "I never considered myself a write-off at all. I always felt confident whatever was happening. But I knew it was more important for everyone for me to get a result this weekend.

"I would have worried a lot more about my results in the first two races if I felt that what happened was all my fault but there were problems with the brakes of the car. I knew it wasn't my fault so I didn't worry too much."

The confident Irvine now hopes to become a serious points-scoring partner to Schumacher and push Ferrari into a position of challenging for the constructors' championship. After three of the season's 17 races they are third with 14 points, behind Williams on 20 and McLaren on 19.

In the drivers' title race, Villeneuve leads with 20 ahead of Briton David Coulthard and Austrian Gerhard Berger who each have 10. Schumacher lies in fifth place with eight points, three places and four points ahead of his 21-year-old brother Ralf who finished third for Jordan on Sunday.

It was Ralf's first podium finish in only his third Grand Prix and in the Jordan team's 100th. "It is a very good result for me and I am really happy," he said. "But it would have been much better if I had not had my accident with my team mate."
Schumacher accidentally knocked Giancarlo Fisichella out of the race on lap 24.
